items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: No, I never heard Emmett play. I wish I had. Of course, my brother-in-law, Steve Lloyd Cannon, banjo player, he said that he played several times with Emmett Hardy.

ctx.x: I want to get back to Dixon in the mist. How did he play on the piano? Did he play more or less legitimately or did he have unusual things?

Well you know, Dixon's piano playing was really amazing because in listening to Dixon's Bix playing piano, I can never really tie in his trumpet with the piano. I don't know if it ever struck you that way, Dick, but listening to his trumpet, it sounds like it's an entirely different phase than his piano playing. His piano sounds so different that it was rhythmical with really sort of modern chords and yet there was the old time flavor along with it. It's just a hard thing to explain, his piano playing. You know,…
Did you ever hear Brownlee's band? Norman Brownlee?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: Emmett Hardy, John, that's something I have heard of. I've often wondered about it. How can you tell? What can you say? I didn't know him.

ctx.x: Well, Herman, where shall we place Emmett Hardy in relation to Bix?

Emmett Hardy, John, that's something I have heard of. I've often wondered about it. How can you tell? What can you say? I didn't know him. No one had a recording of him, did they? I don't think so, did they? I never found him. They said, Monk Hazel said there was a cylinder disc that was made of him, but no one has ever really found it. And Monk Hazel, who I dearly loved as a friend and as a musician, I think Monk really, really knew what he was talking about when he told you something. And Monk said that he…
